population-research.def: In research, the whole group a study wants to draw conclusions about, such as all U.S. high-school seniors.

sample-research.def: The part of a population that is actually studied.

random-sampling.def: Choosing participants so that every member of the population has the same chance of being selected.

representative-sample.def: A sample whose makeup (age, gender, background and so on) matches the population it stands for.

sampling-bias.def: A flaw in how a sample is chosen that makes it unrepresentative, as with a convenience sample of whoever is easy to reach or a self-selected sample of volunteers.

generalizability.def: How far a study’s results can be applied to people beyond its participants; judged by how similar the participants are to the group in question.
